finding: Difference images favour the target in one sector (s77); s49 and s76 are weak_diff. The confirmed rule asks for at least two. The row's own limitation says attribution is limited.
suggested_action: Reconsider tier (probable on the stated rule).

finding: All three sectors are labelled on_target, but the free-fit centroid lies 28-33 arcsec from the target in every sector (more than one TESS pixel), with no capable Gaia neighbour within 90 arcsec.
suggested_action: Look at the difference images; a consistent 30 arcsec offset may point to an uncatalogued or underestimated neighbour.

finding: Labelled on_target in three sectors, but the free-fit offsets are 151.6 and 139.7 arcsec in two of them; only s72 (0.5 arcsec) is within a pixel.
suggested_action: Check whether the two large-offset fits failed; if so only one sector supports the target.

finding: The visual reviewer notes eclipses are absent in s7, s34 and s88 and depth varies 2-6% between sectors, and asks for a human look. s88 is one of the three sectors counted as on_target in the attribution.
suggested_action: Human look before keeping confirmed; an aperture blend would explain sector-dependent depth.

finding: Period refit from 14.240 d to 6.1666 d (ratio 2.309, not a harmonic). Eclipses fall about 1 h after the predicted times. Depth (9.68 ppt vs about 27 ppt in the visual note), event count and period_resolution still describe the old period, and no alternative period is listed.
suggested_action: Refresh the row from the refit and decide whether the ephemeris is secure enough for confirmed.

finding: Adopted period 0.3869 d is twice the photometric 0.1935 d, and the visual note describes two equal ~1.4% minima per orbit in the 2P fold. The methods say two equal minima per orbit at periods under 0.5 d are never above candidate.
suggested_action: Candidate on the stated rule, so out of the count unless the rule is changed.

finding: Adopted period 0.2634 d (twice a refit 0.132 d). The numeric test calls the alternate dips unequal at 5.5 sigma, but the visual note describes two equal ~6.5% V-ish eclipses in the 2P fold.
suggested_action: Decide which reading holds; if the minima are equal the short-period rule caps it at candidate.

finding: depth_ppt is -116.9. The visual note describes 60 ppt eclipses.
suggested_action: Correct the depth.

finding: n_events_prim is 1, but the visual note counts four eclipses in s20. The numeric review rejected the star.
suggested_action: Correct the event count.

finding: secondary_phase is 0.7258, but period_resolution finds the secondary at phase 0.498. depth_ppt is 48.5, against 7-13% in the visual note.
suggested_action: Refresh the secondary and depth columns.

finding: secondary_phase is 0.495, but period_resolution finds the secondary at 0.964. Adopted period 9.764 d; the numeric review had 12.641 d and the visual note suggests a 4.88 d orbit.
suggested_action: Refresh the row; the period is already called unresolved in the reason.

finding: secondary_phase 0.5098 against 0.485 in period_resolution (small).
suggested_action: Minor; refresh if the row is touched.

finding: The visual note says the out-of-eclipse wave suggests ellipsoidal light at a 1.560 d orbit, but the adopted period is 3.120 d and no alternative period is listed. Its secondary is also deeper than its primary.
suggested_action: List 1.560 d as the alternative period.

finding: period_resolution leaves the factor-of-two choice open (equal alternate dips, no secondary, not settled by an SB2 or spectroscopic period), but period_alternative_days is blank. The methods count 83 confirmed systems with an alternative; on these rows' own resolution text the count would be about 92. Some may have been settled on the visual sheet without the row saying so.
suggested_action: Fill the alternative or record how it was settled.

finding: Same as above for probable rows.
suggested_action: Fill the alternative or record how it was settled.

finding: secondary_depth_ppt exceeds depth_ppt by 2-12%, so the epoch marks the shallower eclipse, against the paper's convention that the primary is the deeper. Some rows doubled on visual review already warn about this.
suggested_action: Swap labels or note it per row.

finding: Period refit after the visual review, but period_resolution (and in some rows depth and event counts) still describe the earlier period.
suggested_action: Refresh derived columns for the 28 refit rows.

finding: The target has a Gaia DR3 SB1 or SB2 orbit whose period differs from the eclipse period (possible triple, blend or alias). The confirmed rule does not address this. R1263's doubled period (6.627 d) is 1.7% from Gaia's 6.515 d.
suggested_action: Decide whether a disagreeing Gaia orbit caps the tier, and say so in the methods.

finding: Sectors labelled on_target whose free-fit offset is about 7 arcsec or more: up to about one pixel in most rows, and 33.5 and 68.6 arcsec in one sector of R1182 and R1274. Each row still has at least two on-target sectors within one pixel.
suggested_action: No change needed by the rule; worth one sentence in the methods on how the label relates to the free-fit offset.

finding: Confirmed although the numeric review refuted it (ellipsoidal out-of-eclipse light at least half the depth). This is one of the 72 visual acceptances the methods disclose, and the only one promoted to confirmed from refuted.
suggested_action: None required; noted for transparency.

finding: Saturated stars (Tmag 5.1 and 5.8); the reason says fixed-aperture photometry and difference images are unreliable on bleed columns, yet the attribution reads on_target.
suggested_action: Fine at probable; the attribution label could say saturated.
